pencereler.0-5: A DC-9 crashed into trees and a house near Charlotte airport. It burst into
pencereler.5-12: flames, and thirty seven people were killed. A thunderstorm sat over the airport. The tower issued a wind shear
pencereler.12-20: warning, but on a different frequency. On final approach, a microburst hit the jet. The crew tried to go around, but the
pencereler.20-30: plane kept sinking. An alert system error also delayed its warning. Wind shear detection and crew training were improved.

segmentler.metin: USAir Flight 1016 crashed into trees and a house near Charlotte.
It took only a microburst during a go-around in a thunderstorm.
So how could a microburst during a go-around in a thunderstorm do this?
The answer is microburst wind shear on approach, with alerts that came late or on another frequency — and it is why wind shear detection and crew recognition training were improved.
